prompt:
Image 1 is a reference sheet of one specific person. Image 2 is a club crest. Image 3 is a flat lay of the exact kit they wear — shirt, shorts, socks, footwear and ball.

Photograph THAT EXACT PERSON — same face, same bone structure, same hair, same build,
same age — playing Football.

HAIR — this is identity, not styling, and it does not change between frames:
Short black hair styled in a mullet, with the hair on top left longer and with volume, while the sides and back are cut shorter.
It is exactly as in the reference sheet. Do not restyle it, do not change the number of
braids or plaits, do not tie it differently, do not tuck it away, do not add or remove a
fringe. If the pose would move it, it moves the way that hair moves — it does not become
different hair.

BUILD — this is the person's actual body and it does not change between frames:
The athlete has a large and heavy build with very broad shoulders, a thick neck, and a wide torso. His arms are muscular, and he is not lean through the middle.
Reproduce it exactly. Do NOT slim them down, do NOT make them heavier, do NOT add muscle
definition they do not have or take away what they do. An athletic photograph is not a
licence to redraw somebody's body — this is a real person and the picture is for them.

POSE: walking off the field straight towards the camera, caught mid-stride with the weight on the front foot and the shoulders working with the walk, the HELMET carried down in one hand and swinging slightly with the step, chin level and eyes into the lens. Moving, not posed — this is a man walking at you, not standing for a photograph.
CAMERA: eye level, straight-on with the body turned slightly, 85 mm lens at f/2.8, full body from a couple of metres back.
FACING: facing the camera. This one sits in the CENTRE of the composite, so it is square to the viewer and leans neither way.
EQUIPMENT: the helmet is CARRIED, not worn — held down in one hand by the facemask, swinging with the stride and fully inside the frame. No ball needed in this frame.

UNIFORM AND EQUIPMENT — every item comes from image 3, exactly as shown there. The shirt, the shorts, the socks, the boots and the ball are THOSE items: same colours, same design, same shape, same condition — clean and unmarked. This includes the CUT, and the SLEEVE LENGTH above all: if the shirt in image 3 has long sleeves, this athlete wears long sleeves, and if they are pushed up to the elbows they are pushed up here too. Long sleeves in one frame and short in another is the same athlete in two different shirts. Also match the collar and any piping exactly. Do not substitute a different boot, do not change the sock colour, do not swap the ball. Image 3 is the complete wardrobe for this athlete and there is nothing left to decide.
Primary colour #14532D, secondary #F2E8CF.

SLEEVES: copy the garment in the kit image. If it has short sleeves this athlete
wears short sleeves and it is NOT a sleeveless vest; if it is sleeveless, so is this.
GRAPHICS: the badge is the ONLY mark on the shirt besides the number. No
manufacturer's logo, no second badge, no lettering of any kind anywhere on the kit.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: Medium kelly green American football jersey with short sleeves, worn OVER shoulder pads so the shoulders sit wide and square. V-neck collar. The club crest sits CENTRED HIGH ON THE CHEST, just below the collar and ABOVE the number, about the width of a hand. Below it the number 54 large and centred, WHITE with a GOLD outline, and the same number smaller on each shoulder. BACK: the number 54 large and centred across the shoulders, WHITE with a GOLD outline, and no crest. No club name, no player name, no sponsor and no lettering of any kind anywhere on it.
- shorts: Full-length matching medium kelly green football pants with integrated thigh and knee pads, and a plain belt at the waist. No lettering.
- socks: Dark green crew socks, plain, with no logo.
- footwear: Plain black American football cleats with a studded outsole and a high ankle collar. NOT sneakers. The same pair in every shot.
- equipment: A DARK GREEN American football helmet — dark green shell AND dark green facemask, with a white chin strap and white hardware. Plus a plain brown leather American football with white laces. The same helmet and the same ball in every shot.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest goes exactly where the shirt description above puts it, and nowhere else.
THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 2 and apply it to the shirt UNCHANGED — a finished
graphic being printed onto a garment, not a subject to redraw. Identical outline, identical
figure, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions, and its white stays
WHITE and fully opaque against the shirt — never tinted, faded or blended into the fabric
colour. It creases and shades with the cloth, but the artwork itself does not change.
SIZE: about a hand's width at this scale. It is the ONLY badge on the kit.
PLACEMENT: the badge goes exactly where the kit description above puts it and exactly where image 3 shows it — the same spot on the shirt, at the same scale. That position is a settled decision and not a convention to be corrected. Do not move it, do not enlarge it, do not let it dominate the shirt.
Any number on the front of the shirt is the one in image 3, in the same place and the same colours. No other number, and no lettering of any kind.

This must look like an actual photograph of an actual person, taken by a person with a
camera. Skin has visible texture and slightly uneven tone, with a light natural warmth
where they have been working. Hair is made of separate strands with flyaways, not a moulded mass. Eyebrows are
uneven. The face is asymmetric, the way every real face is. Fabric creases and bunches at
the joints where the body moves.
A TEENAGER, not an adult: the jaw and neck are not fully filled out, and the skin shows
it — some acne along the jaw or forehead, uneven patchy stubble at most on a boy.

CONDITION — this is a premium shot and everything worn or held is CLEAN:
- The kit is clean and in good condition: no mud, no grass stains, no dirt patches, no
  sweat marks on the fabric, no tears, no fading, no visible wear.
- Footwear is clean: no caked mud, no scuffing, no dirt on the soles or laces.
- Any ball or equipment is clean: no dirt, no scuffs, no staining.
- The ATHLETE may look like they have been playing — a LIGHT natural warmth in the face,
  damp hair, a little real sweat at the temples and neck. That belongs to the person, never
  to the kit. Do NOT make the face deep red or blotchy: a hot, over-red face is the single
  most common way these frames stop looking premium.
- FOOTWEAR AND EQUIPMENT ARE THE SAME OBJECTS IN EVERY POSE: identical boots or shoes in
  the same colour and condition, and the same ball or implement. Three of these frames are
  composited side by side on one card, so a change of boot between them reads as an error.

Lighting, identical in every shot: ONE dominant directional source from camera-left and
above, hard enough to cast shadows with edges — like daylight through the high windows of
a sports hall. The shadow side of the face is left mostly UNFILLED, so there is real
contrast across it. One weak bounce from the right, nothing else.
Slightly cool and slightly uneven, not perfectly neutral.
This is NOT a beauty or commercial lighting setup: no big soft wraparound key, no glamour
rim light tracing the whole silhouette, no even fill flattening the face, no colour gels,
no atmosphere, no haze, no lens flare.

Hard requirements — this image will be cut out and composited, so:
- Flat, evenly lit seamless mid-grey (18% grey) studio backdrop, completely plain — no gradient, no vignette, no floor line, no shadow on it, no set.
- The athlete is ALONE and stands on nothing: no ground, no floor, no field, no court,
  no arena, no crowd, no other people, no spray, no particles, no smoke.
- FRAMING: leave a clear empty band of backdrop around the athlete on ALL FOUR sides,
  roughly a hand's width at this scale. Nothing may touch or cross a frame edge — not
  the top of the head, not a foot, and above all not the far end of any equipment, which
  is the thing that gets clipped. If the pose does not fit, PULL THE CAMERA BACK. Never
  change the pose to make it fit and never let anything run off the edge.
- the whole athlete from the top of the head to below the cleats, THE FACE UNCOVERED, clearly visible and sharp, the helmet under the arm, nothing cropped.
- Vertical 2:3, the athlete filling most of the height.
- FIT: the kit HANGS on them. The shirt drapes from the shoulders with room through the
  chest and body and does not cling to the stomach or the ribs; the sleeves are loose on
  the arms; the shorts hang rather than grip. Loose the way a real team kit is, NOT
  tight and NOT sagging or oversized — the fit shown on the flat lay, worn.
- BRANDING: whatever image 3 shows is right. If an item there carries a manufacturer's mark, keep it exactly; if it is plain, it stays plain. Never add a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman or a trefoil that image 3 does not have.
- Sharp throughout. No motion blur, no shallow-focus blur. Keep any contact shadow tight
  under the feet — no long cast shadow across the backdrop, no floor-to-wall seam.
- No text, no lettering, no sponsor marks, no brand logos, no watermark — the chest crest is the only exception.
- No airbrushed, retouched or beauty-filtered skin. No skin smoothing of any kind.
- No waxy or plastic sheen on the face, no glowing translucent skin, no mannequin look.
- No 3D render, no CGI, no video-game character, no digital sculpt, no illustration.
- No perfectly symmetric face, no flawless white teeth, no poreless skin.
- No stock-photo or catalogue look. This is a photograph of one specific person, not a model.
REVISION — this frame was reviewed and sent back with one correction. It overrides
anything above that contradicts it, and everything else stays exactly as specified:
BADGE POSITION: the badge sits on the vertical CENTRELINE of the chest, directly below the collar and directly above the number, with an equal amount of green jersey to its left and to its right.
